newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* The stock market is poised for another slide interspersed with occassional buying by bargain hunters until concerns over the peso end, BPI Securities Corp said.
* "The market is now in an oversold state, and though further dips are expected, bargain hunting may commence in the coming days," Sun Hung Kai Securities said in its market outlook.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index closed 109.46 points lower at 2,589.20, the biggest single-day drop in three months in reaction to renewed speculation that the peso may be devalued.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 119.88 points lower at 7,842.43. PLDT's ADR closed down $5/05 at $62/01.
* The Philippine peso ended unchanged at 26.40 to a dollar.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was at 30.375 percent vs 30.0625 percent.
* The Central Bank on Thursday raised overnight lending rate to 34 percent from 32 and overnight borrowing rate to 32 percent from 30 percent.
* President Fidel Ramos attacked on Wednesday what he said was a foreign campaign to undermine the peso after reports of a possible devaluation battered the country's financial markets.
* The speculative attack on the peso is likely to be short-lived, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said.

* Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson and Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista denied a report by a Singapore-based newspaper that plans to devalue the peso was part of the Monetary Board's agenda in its meeting on Wednesday.

* The Philippines' top five commercial banks raised their prime lending rates to as high as 21 percent following the sharp increase in the Central Bank's overnight rate, bankers said. Metrobank, the largest commercial bank, increased its prime rate to 21 percent from 16 percent last week, a treasury official of the bank said.
* The Central Bank said on Wednesday it was offering 182-day special series Treasury bills at 12.5 percent. The Bank did not offer special series T-bills.
* The Philippine National Bank labour union said it had called off its strike after the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) issued a return-to-work order.
* Philippine car sales in the first six months of this year dropped 7.8 percent to 40,478 units against 43,879 in the year-ago period, the Chamber of Automotive Manufacturers of the Philippines Inc.
* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the Central Bank admitted the continued deterioration of the current account may pose risks to the country's ability to pay its foreign debt.
